walkthrough:
Combine the fractions over the common denominator $\cos\theta(1 + \sin\theta)$:
$$\frac{1 + \sin\theta}{\cos\theta} + \frac{\cos\theta}{1 + \sin\theta} = \frac{(1 + \sin\theta)^2 + \cos^2\theta}{\cos\theta(1 + \sin\theta)}$$

Apply the Pythagorean identity $\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1$ in the numerator:
$$= \frac{1 + 2\sin\theta + 1}{\cos\theta(1 + \sin\theta)} = \frac{2 + 2\sin\theta}{\cos\theta(1 + \sin\theta)}$$

Factor out $2$ in the numerator and cancel the common factor $(1 + \sin\theta)$:
$$= \frac{2(1 + \sin\theta)}{\cos\theta(1 + \sin\theta)} = \frac{2}{\cos\theta}$$

hints: Find solutions in radians on $[0, 2\pi]$ to $3$ significant figures.
walkthrough:
Replace the left-hand side with the identity $\frac{2}{\cos\theta}$:
$$\frac{2}{\cos\theta} = \frac{3}{\sin\theta}$$

Find both solutions in radians on the interval $0 \le \theta \le 2\pi$:
$$\theta = \tan^{-1}(1.5) \approx 0.983\text{ rad}$$
$$\theta = 0.9828 + \pi \approx 4.12\text{ rad}$$
